transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Sonal Gupta (CTO, EdenBridge), Liam O'Connor (ML Engineer), Jared Mills (Infra), Priya Sharma (Product)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand EdenBridge's current mix of OpenAI + self-hosted vLLM/TGI, evaluate parity concerns, and scope a short pilot (hosted or dedicated) to validate latency/cost and generation parity. Security and VPC constraints surfaced; next steps agreed.

Topics:
- Current stack: OpenAI for prod prompts, vLLM for batch and local testing, some TGI experiments
- Parity: generation differences between OpenAI and self-hosted quantized models
- Hosting options: Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Security, KMS, audit logs, SSO
- Benchmarks: latency, cost per token, quality/regression checks

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can do quick intros then get into what you run today and the pain points, is that right?
[00:06] Sonal (EdenBridge): yeah, thanks maya. quick intro from our side - im sonal, cto, we run a mix, prod is mostly openai right now for chat/completion, but we also run vLLM on prem for heavy batch scoring and some offline fine-tune experiments.
[00:18] Liam (EdenBridge): and im liam, ml eng, we built a tgi wrapper for a few collectors, so some models are in tgi, some in vllm, kinda messy.
[00:27] Carlos (Redwood SE): got it. curious — what are your top three blockers migrating away from openai or consolidating?
[00:33] Sonal: parity, for sure. we see subtle output diffs when moving between openai and our local quantized 8bit vllm models — hallucination rates shift, tokenization sometimes off. second is latency p95 for interactive features — need 200-300ms. third is security/compliance, we need SOC2 and kM S compliance, also encryption at rest and audit trails.
[00:51] Maya: good, thats helpful. when you say parity — is that human-eval parity, or deterministic exact-match?
[00:58] Sonal: more quality parity. we have an eval harness — 100 prompts, 10 critical prompts where we need 95% similar outputs or at least same intent. currently openai passes, local vllm is close but not quite.
[01:10] Carlos: that maps to what we see with other customers. a couple of knobs to consider: we can run the same model weights as your openai counterpart if the model is open, run identical tokenizers, and also provide quantization profiles tuned for your workload. parity tests usually include our eval harness + your prompts.
[01:25] Jared (EdenBridge): question — when you say "hosted", is customer data leaving our VPC? we have egress constraints and need to know network topology.
[01:33] Maya: great question. hosted means requests hit Redwood's hosted control plane and inference runtime; we provide options — hosted (multi-tenant), dedicated (reserved GPU pool with isolation), and private (VPC peering or on-prem). for sensitive workloads private gives you a customer-managed control plane or VPC-only path; we can discuss peering and egress rules.
[01:50] Priya (Product): and for function calling and streaming, are those fully supported? we rely on streaming tokens back to UI.
[01:56] Carlos: yes, streaming supported, function/tool calling too. our runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache handling which helps interactive latency. we can tune batch windows to meet your p95 targets.
[02:10] Liam: what's the typical p95 we can hit on something like a 13B quantized model? we need mid 200s or less for snappy UI.
[02:17] Carlos: depends on GPU and batching config. on Dedicated with an A100-style instance and tuned batching we see p95 around 120-250ms for short sequences; hosted varies but we can reserve warm instances. we'll run your traffic shape to get realistic numbers.
[02:31] Sonal: cost is also a big driver. our OpenAI bill is growing; if we can reduce per-token costs by 40-60% but keep quality, that's huge.
[02:39] Maya: understood. typical moves: we show hosted as fastest to try, Dedicated for predictable throughput/cost, Private for compliance. many customers start hosted pilot then switch to dedicated if they need SLA.
[02:50] Liam: about quantization — we currently run 8-bit; people talk about 4-bit and llama.cpp style stuff — will that change outputs?
[02:58] Carlos: yes quantization can shift outputs; our optimize team provides quant profiles and regression tests. for parity we either run fp16 or carefully validated 4-bit/8-bit profiles. we'll include those in the pilot.
[03:11] Sonal: ok, what about model variants? we rely on a few open checkpoints, but openai gives a managed endpoint — how do we map that?
[03:19] Carlos: if model weights are available, we can match them. if youre using closed proprietary models, we can map to nearest open one and evaluate regressions. Redwood supports model catalog and automatic fallback routing to compatible variants for graceful degradation.
[03:33] Jared: security specifics — do you support KMS/HSM, SSO, RBAC, audit logs? we need syslog/ SIEM integration.
[03:40] Maya: yes to the above: KMS integrations, HSM for private deploys, SAML SSO, RBAC, and comprehensive audit logs with export options. we'll share the SOC2/ISO docs and an architecture note for VPC peering.
[03:54] Sonal: do you have customers in finance or healthcare with strict compliance?
[03:58] Maya: yes, several, we have the compliance pack and enterprise support.
[04:02] Liam: for parity testing, can you run a deterministic decode and provide n-best lists so we can compare intent-level results?
[04:09] Carlos: yes, we can run deterministic sampling or temperature 0 and provide n-best. we'll also run token-level diffs and downstream evals.
[04:17] Sonal: what about the eval harness? we can give you our evaluation code, will you run it against Redwood hosted and a dedicated env?
[04:24] Carlos: absolutely, we prefer you to share the harness. we'll run it on hosted first and optionally a dedicated pool. results go into a shared spreadsheet and we highlight regressions and suggestions (quant profiles, tokenizer tweaks).
[04:37] Priya: timeline-wise, we want a pilot before end of august if possible.
[04:42] Maya: sounds doable. next steps: we'll kick off with you sharing eval prompts and usage, we run an initial hosted bench, then discuss dedicated pilot if perf/cost look good.
[04:50] Sonal: ok quick clarifying stuff — data retention, do you keep logs for training or fine-tune?
[04:56] Maya: we do not use customer data to train models by default; retention and logging configurable per account, and we can disable retention for sensitive customers. we'll detail that in the security doc.
[05:05] Jared: will you show us the rollout policies and fallback config? we need automatic fallback to a smaller model if capacity hits.
[05:12] Carlos: yes, rollouts (canary/A-B), automatic fallback to compatible model variants are supported in the console; we can demo that in the next session.
[05:20] Sonal: anything we need to prepare?
[05:22] Maya: please share: (1) 50 sample prompts + 10 eval-critical prompts; (2) representative latency traces and p95/p99; (3) current monthly token usage and cost; (4) redacted sample responses. also confirm VPC constraints.
[05:36] Sonal: we'll get that over.
[05:38] Maya: recap of action items and i'll send a follow-up with links to SOC2 and pilot pricing; then we'll schedule the benchmark run. thanks all.

End of meeting.
